title: Anger Management Therapy and Counseling | Chrysalis Health
description: Individualized anger management therapy for children, teens, adults, and families. Identify triggers, recognize escalation earlier, and build healthier ways to respond. Telehealth available. Call (888) 587-0335.

faq.q: What happens in anger management therapy?
faq.a: A therapist helps identify triggers, warning signs, thought patterns, and behaviors connected to anger. Sessions may address emotional regulation, coping, communication, problem-solving, and conflict-management skills based on the client's needs.

faq.q: How do I know when anger has become a problem?
faq.a: Anger may require professional support when it is frequent, intense, difficult to control, or causing problems with relationships, safety, school, work, or daily functioning.

faq.q: Can therapy help with anger outbursts?
faq.a: Therapy may help a person recognize escalation earlier, understand what contributes to outbursts, and practice safer ways to pause, communicate, and respond. Treatment needs and results vary by person.

faq.q: Is anger management therapy different from an anger management class?
faq.a: Yes. Therapy is individualized mental health treatment based on an assessment and treatment goals. Classes usually follow a standard curriculum and may be required for legal, school, or employment reasons.

faq.q: Can children and teenagers receive anger management counseling?
faq.a: Yes. Counseling can help children and teens recognize emotions, manage reactions, develop coping skills, and communicate more effectively. Parent, caregiver, or family involvement may be included when appropriate.

faq.q: Is online anger management therapy available?
faq.a: Telehealth mental health services may be available depending on the client's location, needs, eligibility, and current program availability. Service options should be confirmed when requesting care.
